content:
maya_support: Customer reported repeated parse failures on /v1/generate with JSON mode. They also saw spikes in tokens billed because client retried on our 5xx. Customer payload attached; says it used to work yesterday. Need triage and temporary mitigation.

infra-bot: alert: 503 on route /v1/generate x-req-id=req_9a7f - upstream parser failure (null-bytes).

sam_ops: grabbing logs now. initial pattern: invalid JSON: unexpected token at offset 1, plus lots of \u0000 in the body. Likely streaming truncation or corrupted client encoding.

eli_devex: quick mitigation we can suggest to the customer: 1) enable client-side exponential backoff + jitter, 2) set `json_mode: "relaxed"` or use our `rescue_parse=true` query param, 3) sanitize control chars before send. Example regex: `payload = payload.replace(/[\u0000-\u001F]/g, '')`

maya_support: Customer wants an ETA for a fix and is asking why billing shows many retries. Do we have a server-side guard to prevent billing on parse-only failures?

raj_eng: short answer: billed tokens are counted once the model emits tokens; our retries are client-driven so they increased invoiced usage. Server can add a pre-parse step to reject obvious garbage at gateway (cheap CPU) -> avoid hitting model. I'll prototyping a gateway sanitizer.

eli_devex: also suggest immediate client-side instructions to reduce cost: lower `max_tokens` to expected output size, set `stop` tokens early, and avoid automatic retry on 4xx/5xx unless it's idempotent. Provide sample retry policy: 
```
// pseudocode
retry(ms=500, attempts=5, factor=1.5, jitter=100) {
  for i in 1..attempts:
    wait = ms * (factor ** (i-1)) +- random(jitter)
    resp = call_api()
    if resp.ok: return resp
    if resp.status in [400,401,403]: break // client error
}
```

sam_ops: reproduction steps I ran: curl with original payload -> immediate parse error. Replacing null bytes with empty string returns valid JSON. Repro notes attached.

maya_support: Customer also reported auth hiccups (short-lived token) earlier today which may have triggered duplicate attempts on client side. Confirmed?

raj_eng: checked logs: their auth token did refresh but with 2xx; timing of retries overlaps. Not our main cause but contributed.

eli_devex: for durable fix we should: 1) Add gateway pre-parse sanitizer to strip control chars and very-long-contiguous-nulls. 2) Add a cheap heuristic to reject payloads > 1MB with an explicit 422 so client doesn't retry. 3) Add optional `rescue_parse` param that attempts a tolerant parse + trimmed output (no charge until model run).

sam_ops: I'll open an RFC and include a small middleware suggestion. For immediate customer-facing note: ask them to run the sanitize regex and switch to the sample backoff.

maya_support: drafting reply to customer now, offering temporary guidance and ETA: sandbox patch to gateway within 48h, full rollout in 5 business days. Will offer invoice credit if we confirm duplicate billing from retries.

raj_eng: I'll take ownership of the prototype. Plan: reproduce with their exact payload, add sanitizer, run canary on dedicated cluster, monitor parse-error rate. If tests pass, auto-deploy to staging -> 24h canary -> gradual rollout.

eli_devex: small extra trick for structured-output: include system message \"You must respond with only JSON matching this schema: ... If you cannot, respond with the single token: \"__PARSE_FAIL__\".\" forces a safe fail path so client can detect parse failures without charging for long outputs.

maya_support: thanks all. I'll send customer instructions and keep them updated. tagging follow-ups: @raj_eng (prototype), @sam_ops (RFC + billing check), @eli_devex (support note + client sample). :white_check_mark:
